summary: The note describes the National Progressive Democrats, a small socialist party in the Republic of Ireland that was active from 1958 to 1963. It was founded as a left-wing, progressive secular party by Noël Browne and Jack McQuillan, both former members of the social democratic wing of Clann na Poblachta.
one_line: A small Irish socialist party active from 1958 to 1963, founded by Noël Browne and Jack McQuillan.
key_facts: The National Progressive Democrats was a small socialist political party in the Republic of Ireland.
The National Progressive Democrats was active between 1958 and 1963.
The National Progressive Democrats was founded as a left-wing progressive secular party.
Noël Browne, a former Minister for Health, was one of the founders of the National Progressive Democrats.
Jack McQuillan was one of the founders of the National Progressive Democrats.
Noël Browne and Jack McQuillan were former members of the social democratic wing of Clann na Poblachta.
The founders of the National Progressive Democrats left Clann na Poblachta before founding the party.
